status: synthetic reversible-network stress test; not an empirical estimate

metric_definitions.Q: Newman-Girvan modularity of the fixed two-camp partition.
metric_definitions.r_x: Pearson correlation of node opinions across oriented edge endpoints.
metric_definitions.phi: Cross-camp conductance; not independent of Q in the planted-cut design.

analytical_bridge_count_result.exact_conditional_drift: 2 * (E[accepted reverse swaps | graph, alpha] - E[accepted homophilic swaps | graph, alpha])
analytical_bridge_count_result.actual_probability_bound: actual repair probability is no larger than the ideal Poisson tail when proposals can fail
analytical_bridge_count_result.ideal_mean_repair_time: ceil(deficit/2)/lambda_minus; a lower bound with feasibility failures
analytical_bridge_count_result.boundary_note: Proposal failures and the simple-graph constraint reduce accepted events; rho_minus=0 makes the cross-edge deficit absorbing under this topology rule.

opinion_noise.law: iid Normal(0, 0.0035^2) added inside the [-1,1] projection after each deterministic update
opinion_noise.stream: dedicated common-random-number stream within each initialization; rewiring uses a separate stream

invariants: All adjacency matrices are simple, undirected, and loop free.
Every stochastic swap preserves each node degree exactly.
Each condition within a seed starts from the same graph and opinion state.
The Hamiltonian-cycle initializer guarantees degree at least two and rewiring preserves that degree sequence.
Reverse rewiring restores mixing toward the initial cross-edge count without restoring edge identities.
